I received the replacement ("Jason" branded) coupling in good order - the shipping/delivery time was less than a week. Upon receipt of this new part, I removed the original (failed) one from the washer motor and transmission shafts, and installed the replacement. It was necessary to lightly tap the coupling end-pieces onto the motor and transmission shafts using a hammer and drive socket, due to the interference fit. I would note that, in my case, the OEM coupling functioned nominally for over 25 years, which is a substantial time period. Also, the old coupling failed in the most typical manner, in which the plastic spikes were sheared off - presumably from cyclic fatigue and aging of the plastic materials.

I acknowledge that there are multiple reviews/comments here that question the quality and design/robustness of the new coupling. Therefore, I would point out that unless it's determined that the original part failed as a result of many cycles of nominal loading and aging, installing a new coupling wouldn't correct the underlying issue. If the transmission or other components in the drive train (excluding the motor itself) have developed excessive friction, this could immediately overload the coupling and cause it to fail again - even with very little use. In this case, it may be that both the original and replacement couplings failure is unrelated to this new component design.

Update June 6: The motor coupling broke again. There weren't any massive loads, in fact it gave out on a small load. The original plastic coupler had simply snapped; the metal insert had stripped out of the plastic on the new coupler.

If you are in need of this part I would recommend checking eBay. I didn't think to look there and searching "whirlpool motor coupling" shows a handful of parts that look to be identical but without the metal insert. Based on my experience the metal insert coupler is a poor design simply because it is made with two materials. The original coupler was entirely plastic and lasted 10+ years, the new one only two weeks.

However if you purchase this part it may last for years, or not if you are unlucky. It may only cost you time and some frustration repairing your washer again. It was a simple fix by replacing the broken piece with the remaining original coupler I had saved.

I have used two different types of these couplings on a 110 washer, at different times. The old full plastic and this "improved" metal-ring version. This one (of which I ordered from Amazon and received an original Whirlpool part) was difficult to install because it required a lot of force to get it on the transmission spindle. I had to use a metal rod and really hammer away at it. I was concerned I might damage the transmission but I left enough room for the washer to move back as I was hammering. Getting it on the motor spindle was easy though it just required a few taps.

In the future I will seek out the full plastic version if I can find any left the next time this breaks. The reason is 1) I really don't like hammering away at the transmission or motor, and 2) the full plastic ones are machined EXACTLY to the right tolerance so you can just slide them on. Then they wear out over time... either the hole that holds the spindle wears down or one of the legs will crack and break off. According to the amazon reviews on this metal ring one it is not exactly improved, since although it prevents the hole from wearing many people report the metal ring just coming right off which isn't any better since the result is the same.

Washing machine back in service. This has metal inserts. I used a socket of the same diameter as the metal insert and a beat-up extension to gently tap into place. Just a guess, but I believe the reviewers that have a problem with insert separation might be hammering the plastic/nylon coupler instead of just the metal insert which probably would lead to premature insert separation from the couplers.

This item is made by Whirlpool, is a factory replacement part and fits my Whirlpool made Kenmore dishwasher like a glove. I was having a problem with the Jet Dry rinse aid completely emptying after only like a week or less after filling it. We run our dishwasher every day with the four of us using so many dishes and glasses. The cap was in good condition, with no cracks or other defects in it or the O-ring of the cap. The only thing I could think of was this dispenser. There would also be a small trickle of dried Jet Dry coming from the dispenser in between loads. Checking around at some of the appliance repair websites, my initial suspicion was confirmed. So I ordered this and installed it.

Looking at the rear of dispenser, a small solenoid releases both the detergent and the drying agent (I imagine at different times in the cycle). My best guess is the solenoid was not closing the valve for the Jet Dry completely. The dishwasher is about 4 1/2 years old now. I have run about 5 full loads through the dishwasher and the fill indicator has hardly moved at all, just like before my problems began, so it looks like I was right about the repair/replacement.

**Edit 8/18/13** I'm getting about a month to six weeks out of a full load of Jet Dry now, that's with using the dishwasher almost every day. This is still working great, I know now that my initial assessment was correct.

I received the ordered detergent dispenser very promptly, and at first glance it appeared to be the perfect replacement for my dispenser that had a broken door latch. However, when comparing the old with the new, it was immediately clear that the electrical connectors were completely different and that if I didn't take matters into my own hands the new one couldn't be used. Fortunately, I was able to remove the plunger unit (that opens the dispenser at the right time during the wash cycle) from the old unit and install it in the new unit. Having done that, the replacement was fast and effective. All I can say is that having supplied Whirlpool with the model and serial number of the dishwasher, I am a bit surprised that they shipped me a new dispenser that was not compatible with the existing wiring.
